title: 5 Simple Hacks
subtitle: // build websites with AI that don't look AI-made

sections.heading: Why AI Websites All Look The Same
sections.body: Most AI-built landing pages fail for the same reason: one vague prompt, zero constraints, and a model hallucinating taste. The result is generic gradients, interchangeable copy, and a hero section that could belong to literally anyone.

sections.heading: The Workflow That Fixes It
sections.body: Better websites do not come from better luck. They come from a better pipeline.

sections.heading: Hack 1: Write The Brief Once
sections.body: Do not start with, build me a website. Start with a persistent brief that tells the AI who this is for, what the brand feels like, what the stack is, and what good looks like.
bulletPoints: Rules the AI should follow every pass

codeSnippet.code:
# project-brief.md or CLAUDE.md
- Build a premium landing page for a local business
- Use warm neutrals and one accent color
- Avoid generic SaaS gradients and fake dashboards
- Prioritize clear hierarchy, strong CTA, mobile polish
- Review spacing, typography, and copy before finishing

sections.heading: Hack 2: Add Taste On Purpose
sections.body: AI is good at remixing patterns, not inventing taste. So give it a design skill, a design system, reference pages, or explicit visual constraints before it writes front-end code.
bulletPoints: Name the vibe precisely, not vaguely
Call out what to avoid, not just what to include

quote.text: I spend less time figuring things out through trial and error, and more time making sure my code is secure and performant.
quote.author: Claudio Wunder

sections.heading: Hack 3: Feed Assets, Not Adjectives
sections.body: Saying modern and professional gets you a site that looks like everyone else's. Upload the logo, palette, typography, screenshots, product copy, and any brand guide you have. Concrete inputs beat poetic prompting every time.

sections.heading: Build A Context Stack
sections.body: The best outputs come from layered context, not from one magic sentence.

sections.heading: Hack 4: Build In Passes
sections.body: Do not ask for the final site in one shot. Ask for structure first, then styling, then copy polish, then responsive cleanup, then bug fixes. AI does better when the creative direction is sequenced.

codeSnippet.code:
1. Build the page structure only. No styling pass yet.
2. Now restyle it using the attached brand guide and logo.
3. Rewrite the hero and CTA for a premium local-service audience.
4. Tighten spacing, fix mobile layout, and remove generic filler copy.
5. Review the page like a creative director and list remaining issues.

sections.heading: Hack 5: Review Like A Creative Director
sections.body: Your job is no longer typing every div by hand. Your job is judging what deserves to stay on the page. Cut weak copy. Fix spacing. Push hierarchy. Make the AI earn every section.

sections.heading: This Works Beyond One Tool
sections.body: Claude Code, v0, Lovable, Bolt, whatever. The tool matters less than the workflow. In 2026, the teams shipping the best AI-built sites are the ones supplying better context and doing better review.
bulletPoints: Use the builder that fits your stack
Keep the brief and assets reusable
Treat AI as fast execution, not final judgment

sections.heading: The Takeaway
sections.body: Five simple hacks. Write the brief once. Add taste on purpose. Feed assets, not adjectives. Build in passes. Review like a creative director. That is how you use AI to build websites that look branded instead of vibe-coded.
